senses.d: To be in harmony about an opinion, statement, or action; to have a consistent idea between two or more people.
ex: All parties agree in the expediency of the law.
I mostly agree with what you said, but I consider your last point to be unfair.

senses.d: To give assent; to accede.
ex: It was agreed to meet here at midday.
The workers did not agree to the new terms offered by the trade union.

senses.d: To yield assent to; to approve.
ex: We agreed a bargain yesterday.
The essential idea is that parties should enter the market, choose their contractors, set their own terms and agree a bargain.

senses.d: To make a stipulation by way of settling differences or determining a price; to exchange promises; to come to terms or to a common resolve; to promise.
ex: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?

senses.d: To resemble; to coincide; to correspond; to tally.
ex: The picture does not agree with the original.
The two scales agree exactly.

senses.d: To suit or be adapted in its effects; to do well.
ex: The same food does not agree with every constitution.

senses.d: To correspond to (another word) in a grammatical category, such as gender, number, case, or person.
ex: In Romanian, all articles, adjectives, and pronouns agree in gender, number and case with the noun they refer to.

senses.d: To consent to a contract or to an element of a contract.
